meta.note: Plain-language explanations for readers who are new to the terms. They are summaries, not the legal definitions: the instrument named under 'See' governs.

terms.full: Securities and Exchange Board of India
terms.def: The securities market regulator, set up under the SEBI Act, 1992. It registers intermediaries, makes regulations, inspects and investigates, and can penalise breaches.
The rulebook every listed entity follows after listing: board and committee rules, disclosures to stock exchanges, results, shareholding pattern and related party transactions.

Information about a listed company or its securities that is not generally available and would likely affect the share price if it were, such as results, dividends, mergers or major changes in management.
A connected person, or anyone in possession of or with access to UPSI. Insiders may not trade while holding UPSI.
An employee or connected person whom the company's board names, by role and access to UPSI, as covered by its insider trading code of conduct.
The period when designated persons may trade. It closes from the end of each quarter until 48 hours after the results are published.
A pre-set plan an insider files and discloses in advance so that trades can go through even while the insider holds UPSI. A cool-off period of 120 calendar days applies.
The record a listed company or intermediary keeps of everyone with whom UPSI has been shared, with time stamps.
An event or information a listed entity must disclose to the stock exchanges. Some are always material (Schedule III Para A); others are tested against the materiality criteria in regulation 30.
A transfer of resources, services or obligations between a listed entity and a related party. Material ones need prior shareholder approval.
A listed entity with listed non-convertible debt of Rs 5,000 crore or more outstanding. It follows the LODR corporate governance rules on a comply-or-explain basis.
Debt securities and non-convertible redeemable preference shares that do not convert into equity, such as NCDs.
A fund a debt issuer sets up with the stock exchange so the debenture trustee can meet the costs of enforcing security on default.
A SEBI-registered entity that protects debenture holders: it monitors security and asset cover and acts on default.
The exchange platform through which private placements of debt above the set size are bid and allotted.
An offer an acquirer must make to the public shareholders of a listed company on crossing the takeover thresholds, normally for at least 26% of the shares.
Buying up to 5% more of a listed company's voting rights in a financial year without an open offer, allowed for a holder of 25% or more.
Every listed company other than a public sector company must keep at least 25% of its shares with the public.
The share of post-issue capital, at least 20%, that promoters must hold after an IPO. It is locked in for 18 months, or three years in some cases.
The company that runs a mutual fund's schemes under the supervision of the trustees.
The trustee company that holds a mutual fund's property in trust for unitholders and supervises the AMC.
All the expenses charged to a mutual fund scheme's investors as a share of its assets. Only the categories allowed by the MF Regulations may be charged.
A charge on redemption of mutual fund units. It goes back to the scheme and cannot exceed 3% of NAV for an open-ended scheme.
The value of one unit of a mutual fund scheme, computed every day from the scheme's net assets.
A category under the MF Regulations 2026 that lets a mutual fund run investment strategies with more flexibility than ordinary schemes, for investors who meet the set thresholds.
A lighter mutual fund route under Chapter X of the MF Regulations 2026 for passive schemes such as index funds and ETFs.
A privately pooled fund registered with SEBI that invests for its investors. Category I and II funds are close ended; Category III may be open or close ended.

An investor whose income, net worth or securities market exposure meets the AIF Regulations' thresholds and who is accredited by an agency or, since October 2026, by a specified manager. Some minimum investment rules do not apply to them.
The offer document of an AIF scheme. Compliance with its terms is audited every year.
The minimum stake an AIF's manager or sponsor must keep in the fund: the lower of 2.5% of corpus or Rs 5 crore (5% or Rs 10 crore for Category III).
A member of a recognised stock exchange registered with SEBI to trade for clients or on its own account.
A member of a clearing corporation that clears and settles trades for itself (self-clearing) or for other brokers.
A stock broker that SEBI designates because of its size, client base and market impact, with extra obligations on governance and systems.
The periodic return to clients of the funds a stock broker holds for them, as the Stock Brokers Master Circular specifies.
The short statement of key terms a stock broker gives clients when opening an account.
An agency that holds clients' KYC records so that one KYC works across securities market intermediaries.
The integrity, reputation and competence test that every SEBI intermediary and its key people must meet at all times.
SEBI's online system for investor complaints against listed companies and intermediaries. Complaints must be resolved within 21 calendar days.
The Smart ODR portal for disputes between investors and listed companies or intermediaries: online conciliation first, then online arbitration.
SEBI's cyber security framework for regulated entities, graded by size. Cyber incidents must be reported within 6 hours.

Closing SEBI enforcement proceedings by paying a settlement amount and meeting other terms, without admitting or denying the findings. Governed by the 2026 Settlement Regulations from 7 November 2026.
The SEBI officer who holds an inquiry and imposes penalties under the SEBI Act.
The tribunal that hears appeals against SEBI orders. An appeal must be filed within 45 days.
An order to give up profits made, or losses avoided, through a breach of securities law. SEBI can direct it under s. 11B of the SEBI Act.
